title: Chicken Light Soup
author: Cynthia Prah
desc: Everything into the pot at once, boiled hard twenty minutes, then the aromatics lifted out and blended back — and torn basil at the end.
longDesc: The simplest documented light soup, and the only one credited to a named home cook with a named narrator: everything goes into the pot together — a whole soup chicken, four tomatoes, two onions, garlic, chillies, ginger and a litre and a half of water — and boils hard for twenty minutes. Then the tomato, onion, garlic, chilli and ginger are removed, blended and returned, and the soup cooks on until the chicken is tender. A small handful of torn basil goes in at the end, off the boil, which no other version includes.
ingredients: 2 tsp chicken stock, or fish, beef or vegetable
A small handful of torn basil
Vegetables, other meats, fresh or smoked fish
steps: Combine everything except the basil in a pot.
Remove the tomato, onion, garlic, chilli and ginger.
Blend them smooth and return them to the pot.
Cook until the chicken is tender.
Lower the heat, stir in the torn basil, and simmer a few minutes.
chefTips: A soup chicken, not a roasting bird — an older, tougher hen with enough collagen to give the broth body. It is the single biggest difference between a good light soup and a thin one.
Everything in at once, twenty minutes on high. The blending-and-returning happens afterwards, which is simpler than the marinate-first method and gives a very similar soup.
Torn basil at the end, off the boil. It is unique to this version among the documented light soups and it lifts the whole pot.
Blend the aromatics smooth and sieve them if you want it genuinely clear. This version does not sieve, so it is slightly thicker than a market light soup.
Until the chicken is tender, which for a real soup chicken can be a long time. The twenty minutes is only the first stage.
The stock is given as two teaspoons of powder or cube. With a proper soup chicken you can leave it out entirely.
Fresh or smoked fish is offered as an addition. Smoked fish turns this into a different and very good soup, but add it late — it falls apart.
commonMistakes: Boiling the basil rather than stirring it in off the heat.
Skipping the remove-blend-return step and just simmering everything.
Stopping at twenty minutes, before the chicken is tender.
Adding smoked fish at the start, so it disintegrates.
sources: Adapted from 'Light Soup', My African Food Map, a project of Tuleka Prah, africanfoodmap.com. CREDIT AS PRINTED: recipe courtesy of Cynthia Prah, with narration by Mr Nkansah, both from Accra. Yield as printed: 4-6 servings. NO DATE is shown on the page. This is the only documented light soup credited to a named home cook rather than to a publication or a lab.

Ingredients exactly as printed: 4 large tomatoes; 2 medium onions; 3 cloves garlic; 2 chillies; 1 root ginger; 1 whole soup chicken, chopped; Salt and pepper to taste; 2 teaspoons chicken stock (or fish/beef/vegetable); Small handful torn basil; 1.5 litres water; Optional: vegetables, other meats, fresh or smoked fish.

Method as printed: combine everything in a pot and boil on high 20 minutes; remove the tomato, onion, garlic, chilli and ginger, blend and return; cook until the chicken is tender; lower the heat, stir in the basil, and simmer a few minutes.

THE BASIL is unique to this version among all the light soups consulted and is the reason it is published separately rather than merged with GHA011. No other source includes a fresh herb at the finish.
'1 root ginger' and 'small handful torn basil' are not quantities and have NOT been converted into any. They are reproduced as printed.
DONENESS CUE: 'until the chicken is tender'. No sensory endpoint beyond that and the initial 20 minutes.

DISAGREEMENT WITH THE OTHER DOCUMENTED LIGHT SOUP, unreconciled: this version boils everything together from the start; Time Out Accra (GHA011) marinates the meat in a blended paste first, cooks it gently, then adds water. Water also differs sharply — 1.5 litres here for a whole chicken against 500 ml there for 500 g of goat. Both are published as printed.

ON THE PROJECT: My African Food Map is Tuleka Prah's documentation project, which records recipes from named cooks with named narrators. That structure is why the credit here runs to two people rather than a byline, and it is reproduced as the page gives it.
For the lab-standardised light soup figures and the byline conflict on a third source, see the sources at GHA011; they are not repeated here.
reheating: Simmer gently. Add fresh basil rather than relying on the cooked-in leaves.
healthBenefits: A long-simmered whole chicken gives collagen and minerals that a breast-only broth does not.
High in protein and very low in carbohydrate.
Basil contributes eugenol and other aromatic antioxidants.
culturalNote: That this recipe comes with a narrator as well as a cook is worth noticing — it was recorded as someone describing how they make it, which is why it reads as a sequence of plain actions rather than a tested formula. The basil is the kind of detail that only survives when a recipe is taken down from a person rather than compiled from other recipes.
